text: The Patriots' catastrophic 1-2 start has become impossible to ignore, with Drake Maye's early-season struggles front and center after the offense managed just 9.7 points per game—dead last in the NFL—and suffered a humbling 35-6 blowout loss to Jacksonville that included two Maye interceptions and a lost fumble, prompting the quarterback to call the performance "unacceptable" and vow to look within himself for answers rather than blame his right shoulder, which he insists hasn't affected his throwing ability. The offensive line infrastructure around Maye took another hit Tuesday when guard Greg Van Roten was placed on injured reserve with a thigh injury, leading the team to sign rookie offensive lineman Da'Metrius Weatherspoon to the practice squad in hopes of shoring up protection, while questions swirl about whether the Patriots are utilizing their young quarterback correctly in Mike Vrabel's system. As New England prepares to travel to Buffalo for Sunday's 1 p.m. ET kickoff at Highmark Stadium, the pressure mounts on both Maye and the offense to demonstrate that their early woes represent a fixable execution problem rather than a systemic one.
